text: The account of Tariq Mirza (PK**HABB****4318) shows a pattern of frequent cash deposits that collectively exceed the daily cash transaction reporting threshold (PKR 500,000) and are made across multiple branches within a short period. From 4 March to 28 March 2026, the customer deposited a total of PKR 12,842,000 in cash, with individual deposits ranging from PKR 221,000 to PKR 1,986,000. The deposits were made at the DHA Phase 6 Branch on several occasions (e.g., 5 March PKR 986,000; 6 March PKR 885,000; 9 March PKR 1,946,000; 10 March PKR 734,000; 11 March PKR 302,000; 13 March PKR 1,701,000; 16 March PKR 707,000; 21 March PKR 690,000; 22 March PKR 882,000; 23 March PKR 726,000; 25 March PKR 1,880,000; 27 March PKR 428,000; 27 March PKR 221,000; 28 March PKR 719,000). These deposits are well below the CTR threshold individually but collectively indicate structuring (smurfing) to avoid detection. Additionally, the account has outbound transfers to entities such as Al-Noor Exchange Company (PKR 3,617,000 on 7 March) and Sheraz Traders (PKR 817,000 on 12 March), suggesting possible conversion of cash into other forms. The alert system flagged repeated cash deposits within 20% below the CTR threshold and cash deposits across branches in 30 days, with a typology score of 320 exceeding the alert threshold of 300. Given the volume, frequency, and pattern of cash deposits, this activity warrants filing a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR).
